title: US v. Google ad-tech — redaction-motion deadline; the sealed remedies opinion unseals automatically if nobody moves (E.D. Va.)
source: NEWS: ppc.land, 'DOJ loses AdX divestiture bid as Brinkema accepts behavioral remedies' (fetched direct 2026-09-08), quoting the 2026-09-02 order: 14 days for the parties to move for redactions to the sealed Memorandum Opinion, and if no motion is filed by that date 'the opinion is unsealed automatically'. Corroborated on the 14-day sealing period by TechCrunch, 'Google spared from ad-business breakup, but judge orders changes to how it operates' (fetched direct 2026-09-08), which reports the written ruling 'would remain sealed for 14 days to permit redactions'. Underlying docket entry in United States et al v. Google LLC, No. 1:23-cv-00108 (E.D. Va.), never fetched. Filed estimate: no confirmed prefix exists for a federal court docket (the market-events-data.ts schema gap), this lane may not self-confirm an in-sweep discovery, and the informative branch here is CONDITIONAL — the deadline is date-certain, the unsealing is not. Checked 2026-09-08
notes: Tiered `low` on the conditionality, not on the subject matter. The date is hard, but what happens on it is a fork: either party moving for redactions (the likely branch — the opinion covers confidential auction mechanics and commercial terms) pushes the public reasoning out by an unknown interval, and only the no-motion branch publishes it on this date. A `low` row that resolves upward is the honest tier for a checkpoint whose payload may not arrive; the operative terms have their own dated row anyway (google-adtech-final-judgment-2026-10-02). Two collisions worth stating: 2026-09-16 is FOMC decision day (fomc-2026-09-16, `confirmed`, a coin-flip hike priced ~52-59% as of 09-08), so anything published that afternoon lands in a session no single-name read survives; and it falls two weeks BEFORE the goog-2026-10-28-print D-20 entry close (2026-09-30), which is the one useful thing about it — it is the last scheduled chance for the ad-tech terms to become public while that pre-print long is still unopened, rather than while it is running. Discovered during the goog-2026-10-28-print pulse check, 2026-09-08 (adjacency sweep item 4, policy/legal).
